description: Orange PVC traffic cone with a square weighted black base and one white reflective collar.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standard orange PVC traffic cone with a square black rubber base, a single wide white reflective collar around the upper third and a rounded tip Materials: Faded orange PVC with road dust, the reflective collar scuffed and peeling at one edge, black base worn grey at the corners.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 960/2,000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, two 256 px canvases -- the whole of this round cost nothing on any axis. Both things the 0.90 verdict named have moved: the cone body carries streaking, low-frequency cloud mottle and near-black tyre rubs, and the collar is on its measurement instead of 26 luma over it. What is still absent is the collar's TORN TAPE EDGE, which is geometry rather than surface and would cost the sleeve's lathe its second ring.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 0.38 x 0.702 x 0.38 m; band table vs the proxy: mean |delta width| 0.0073, |delta depth| 0.0073, nine of ten bands within 0.01 H; band 0 +0.016 is the declared base width over the proxy's 0.354.

Sleeve 0.37-0.555 m, 4 mm proud, visible at 0, 90, 180, 270. Tone MEASURED against the plate over a matched band (0.22-0.32 of the silhouette, middle fifth of its width): plate 186/168/163, luma 173 at saturation 0.12; shipped 188/170/164, luma 174 at 0.13.
featureReviews.notes: It was #c4c4c2 off region-collar and rendered 199 at saturation 0.01 -- a clean white sleeve on a cone that has stood in traffic, and 26 luma over the reference. The harness returns this material almost exactly as authored (196 in, 199 out), so the correction was a straight authoring of the measurement: #baa8a3 came back 192/180/176 and #b49c96 lands on it. The plate's torn tape edge is still not modelled.

featureReviews.evidence: Square chamfered slab as a 4-segment lathe, now reading as DARK RUBBER with pale weathered patches instead of the pale grey slab the first build shipped. Three things were wrong together: the envelope was #6e6b67 (luma 106) with the dark only reaching #524e4a (79), and the harness's additive term returned ~140 on screen; the wash was the grime tile's default bottom-up GRADIENT, which on a horizontal slab maps straight across the face and split it into a pale half and a dark half with a hard seam; and the pale scuffs had nowhere to come from. The envelope is the pale scuff now (#7d7a76), the wash is FLAT, and the scuffs are patches where the wash is erased back toward white -- the only way a multiply tile can put pale wear on a dark base.
featureReviews.notes: Then measured against the plate over the matched slab band (bottom 6% of the silhouette, middle 70% of its width): plate 77/76/73, luma 76 at saturation 0.05; the build read 69/61/52, luma 63 at 0.25 -- 13 counts too DARK on top of the chroma the gate forces. A straight 1.20x on the dark tone (#332b21 -> #3e352a) lands it at luma 76 exactly, saturation 0.25. The neutrality cannot be closed and is recorded as the gate's price: the plate's charcoal is saturation 0.05 at luma 76, squarely inside the turntable gate's 34..82 backdrop window, so an enclosed slab top authored neutral is read as a hole punched through the model. Held against the turntable gate on CHROMA: at #2e2a24 (sat 0.22, which renders at roughly 0.75 of the authored value and lands on the gate's 0.16) the slab was flagged at up to 1,542 px. #332b21 carries 0.35 and measures 0/223/1/0 px across the four azimuths. #37291a also passed but read visibly brown against a plate whose base is neutral charcoal.

name: Traffic Cone
notes: The cheapest prop in the kit and one of the most repeated: rows of them line every roadworks and market street. Convex collider rather than box so it can be knocked over believably. Not breakable.
